stem: An analytics company's clients across multiple continents upload large multi-gigabyte files directly to a single S3 bucket in one Region, and uploads from clients far from that Region are consistently slower because of the physical distance the traffic must travel.

choices.text: Split each upload into more multipart upload parts
Use byte-range GET requests against the uploaded objects
Spread the uploads across additional S3 key prefixes
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket

rationale: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes an upload through the nearest CloudFront edge location and over AWS's backbone network instead of the public internet, cutting the latency caused by the physical distance between a distant client and the bucket's Region. Adding more multipart upload parts parallelizes a single object's own upload but does not address the added latency of crossing the public internet to reach a distant Region. Byte-range GET requests parallelize a download of an existing object, not an upload of a new one. Spreading uploads across additional key prefixes raises the request-rate ceiling for a high volume of concurrent requests, but it does nothing about the distance-driven latency any single distant client experiences.
